note: Willim et al. (2024) describes the primary cohort of 33 individuals with dominant LRRC7 variants presenting with ID, autism, ADHD, and aggression, making the evaluation of formal ASD diagnostic frequency vs broader autistic traits coherent and grounded.

evidence.text: Willim et al. characterized 33 individuals with neurodevelopmental disorder caused by heterozygous LRRC7 variants, where the clinical spectrum included intellectual disability, autism, ADHD, aggression, and abnormal eating behaviors.

source.title: Variants in LRRC7 lead to intellectual disability, autism, aggression and abnormal eating behaviors
source.quote: We identify here 33 individuals (one of them previously described) with a dominant neurodevelopmental disorder due to heterozygous missense or loss-of-function variants in LRRC7. The clinical spectrum involves intellectual disability, autism, ADHD, aggression and, in several cases, hyperphagia-associated obesity.

evidence.text: Khan et al. note that LRRC7 variants were previously described in 33 individuals displaying developmental delay, language impairment, seizures, and autism.

source.title: Further Evidence for LRRC7 Gene Involvement in Neurodevelopmental Disorder: A Novel Variant
source.quote: LRRC7 variants were reported in 33 individuals with developmental delay, language impairment, seizures, autism
